text:
This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with contrasting emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph, or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s matchwinner, Deniz Gul, came away with worse than that, needing treatment after taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as he scored from a corner on 77min, the game’s first effort on target.
Galatasaray maintained their commanding home form to extend Villa’s winless run to six in all competitions. A livid Unai Emery was booked for protesting to match officials as a low-quality game on a poor pitch ticked past five minutes of stoppage time.
History showed this was never going to be an easy hurdle for Villa. The Turkish champions have dropped points here once since the opening day of the season, a Champions League defeat against Barcelona last month. Galatasaray have now been beaten just once in 11 home meetings with Premier League opposition, with Arsenal, in 2014, the last English side to emerge victorious. Galatasaray beat Liverpool 1-0 here in last season’s round of 16 in March, before a comprehensive defeat at Anfield in the second leg. Eventually, in typically noisy, hostile surroundings, they overcame Villa by the same scoreline.
Villa had appeared generally comfortable despite the racket raining down from the stands. Taylor Harwood-Bellis looked strong on his first Champions League start. But Villa did not fashion their first opening – and first shot on goal – until a couple of minutes after going behind, the substitute Ibrahim Mbaye forcing Ugurcan Cakir into a save. While the assistant referee flagged the Senegal winger offside, replays suggested he may have been onside.
Emery insisted the pitch would not affect his team selection and so he made four changes from Saturday’s stalemate with Sunderland, his captain, John McGinn, returning to the XI together with Tyrone Mings, João Gomes and the fit-again Victor Lindelöf. Gomes was booked for a cynical foul on Yunus Akgun approaching the hour, a few minutes after McGinn was cautioned for a barge on Aleksei Batrakov, the 21-year-old Russia midfielder. A melee ensued close to the touchline but the referee, Daniel Siebert, was quick to defuse tensions.
